title: Recurring approved-work reconciliation
goal: On recurrence, answer which reported work was genuinely approved and remains unimplemented, without re-reading the report corpus.
success_condition: The verifier confirms that every report whose content hash changed since the last accepted iteration has been reclassified from its own decision and implementation evidence, and that the resulting delta is either empty or emitted with per-item citations.

trigger.predicate: The content hash of the report-corpus inventory differs from the hash recorded by the last accepted iteration.

preconditions.description: Every report path in the inventory is readable and its hash is computable. An unreadable member is an integrity fault, never an implicit empty.

All three approval sources are reachable: ruling documents, backlog task notes, and the durable record of chat-issued instructions. An unreachable source is an integrity fault and never a proposed-never-approved verdict.
The implementation HEAD used to judge landed work is resolvable, so delivered-but-not-in-the-working-tree cannot read as unimplemented.
The referenced research-approved-work skill and its deterministic scanner are installed and runnable.

permitted_actions: read the report-corpus inventory and its metadata
write the derived index owned by the referenced skill
emit a delta report for firstmate to relay
forbidden_actions: implement any work the scan finds
close, reopen or edit any backlog item or decision
edit, move or delete any report
open, push to or merge any pull request
spawn, steer or tear down any worker
treat a finding as authorization to change code

required_evidence: corpus inventory hash for this iteration and the previous accepted one
per-report content hash and size for every changed member
per-item citation naming the approval source and its location
per-item implementation evidence resolved against a named HEAD
the count of corpus members skipped as unchanged

terminal_states.name: no_delta
terminal_states.description: The corpus is unchanged since the last accepted iteration. Reaching this must cost no model turn.

terminal_states.name: delta_emitted
terminal_states.description: The corpus changed and a cited delta was emitted for firstmate to relay.

terminal_states.name: confirmed_work_found
terminal_states.description: At least one item is confirmed approved and still unimplemented, with approval and implementation proven separately.

terminal_states.name: needs_ruling
terminal_states.description: An item's approval or supersession cannot be settled from evidence and requires a captain ruling. The loop stops rather than guessing.

terminal_states.name: blocked_by_evidence_integrity
terminal_states.description: A corpus member or decision source was unreadable, so absence of evidence could not be distinguished from evidence of absence.

terminal_states.name: budget_exhausted
terminal_states.description: An iteration, wall-clock or capacity budget was reached before the success condition was met.

terminal_states.name: verification_failed
terminal_states.description: The verifier ran and rejected the iteration, or was unavailable. An unavailable verifier lands here and can never become a pass.

terminal_states.name: no_progress_stalled
terminal_states.description: Consecutive iterations produced no verifier-declared progress, so the loop stopped instead of repeating forever.

escalation.authority_owner: firstmate, escalating to the captain where the authority contract requires it
escalation.channel: the task's durable status record, never a worker pane

idempotency.claim_scope: At most one open iteration per (spec id, event key). A repeated wake carrying an already-claimed key is refused and mutates nothing.

evidence.written_to: the derived, content-addressed index owned by the research-approved-work skill

notes: This spec is ready_not_active and cannot become enabled today, for two independently sufficient reasons the validator enforces rather than asserts: its trigger has no implemented detector and no verified execution path, and its only permitted skill is not installed. It deliberately references research-approved-work instead of restating that skill's workflow, so the scan procedure keeps exactly one owner. Whether the capacity stop band covers validation runs is an open captain decision owned by another lane; capacity_stop_band_percent bounds starting a new iteration only, and never blocks verifying an iteration already in flight.
